mappings.note: Listing the government departments whose boards one passes, and what each does. LO-115 is a direct fit - reporting on the functioning of a government office in one's own locality. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)
Gandhi's gram swaraj of self-sufficient village republics. LO-109, which distinguishes local government from State government; LO-106 is rejected because the point is the tier, not equality.

Majority dominance checked by the rule of law and a Constitution protecting minority rights. LO-106, the significance of equality in a democracy; LO-107 is rejected as no kinds of equality are distinguished.
Why police must stay inside constitutional limits - unchecked force would threaten the liberty of the citizens they protect. Equal protection under law, LO-106.
@RailwaySeva on X as a channel to reach the Railways. LO-113, the role of media in a democracy, here in its social-media form.
Why local matters belong to local decision-makers - proximity to the problem and to workable solutions. LO-109, local against State government.

Listing achievements and outstanding problems in one's own place and naming the tier responsible. LO-109 for attributing each to a level of government, LO-108 for interpreting issues in one's own region.
Reading newspaper editorials and counting how many take a position on government policy. LO-113, the role of media in a democracy. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)

'Every democracy is a republic' tested against the UK, Canada and Sweden. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the working of democracy and its institutions; no LO covers forms of state, LO-106 being about equality.
Two reasons decentralisation matters in India. LO-109, local against State government. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)

A student council used to test power-sharing, the limits of authority over food and language, and what unchecked power does. CG-SST3 for the working of democratic institutions, LO-106 for the equal voice the answer rests on.
Three tiers - Union, State, local. LO-109 exactly.

The political executive as the elected Prime Minister, Chief Ministers and cabinets. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the institutions of Indian democracy; LO-109 is rejected because the item spans tiers rather than distinguishing them.

Permanent executive of career civil servants against a political executive that changes with elections. CG-SST3 for the institutional distinction, LO-115 because the permanent executive is what staffs the offices that LO addresses.
Bureaucrats advising, implementing and delivering public services. LO-115 for the working of a government office, CG-SST3 for its place among the organs of government.

Mapped on its stem, which asks which service C.B. Muthamma was the first Indian woman to join. LO-112, the causes and consequences of disadvantages faced by women. (The options and answer stored here belong to a question about a state's permanent population; see report.)
State as the permanent entity, government as the changeable system running it. Goal-level CG-SST3 for a foundational political concept; no LO reaches it.
Concurrent subjects such as education and marriage handled by the Union along with the States. Allocation of subjects between tiers, LO-109.
Differences between democratic, monarchic, theocratic, dictatorial and oligarchic government. Goal-level CG-SST3; the frame's LOs cover equality, tiers and elections, not the typology of regimes.
Why India has three tiers rather than one. LO-109 exactly, the distinction between levels of government.
Who to approach for a broken streetlamp or a village road - ward councillor, Gram Panchayat, Zila Parishad, not the Centre. LO-109 for the tier, LO-115 for the office one actually goes to.

This row's stem is several questions run together; the scored content is what its answer resolves - C.B. Muthamma as the first woman into the Indian Foreign Service in 1949. LO-112, women's position and the barriers to it. (Merged stem; see report.)

Democracy as rule by the people through free and fair elections. CG-SST3 for the working of democracy, LO-106 for the equal say that definition rests on; LO-110 is rejected because no election process is described.
The Dongria Kondh using consent laws to stop mining in their sacred hills. LO-108 is a direct fit - interpreting a social and economic issue in a region with reference to rights.
CPGRAMS as the portal for lodging grievances about public services. LO-115, how a government office works and how a citizen reaches it.

Asking family how they dealt with government over a year and sorting the instances by tier. LO-115 for the encounters with offices, LO-109 for the classification by level. (Empty answer on this row; see report.)
The state as a permanent political organisation with authority over a defined territory and population. Goal-level CG-SST3; no LO covers the concept of the state.
Sovereignty as the power to make law without outside interference. Goal-level CG-SST3, same reasoning.
The school analogy - the state is the school, the government the principal and teachers. Goal-level CG-SST3.

George Washington refusing a crown in 1782. Commitment to a republican form of government; goal-level CG-SST3, and CG-SST2 is rejected because the chapter uses it to illustrate a constitutional principle, not to teach American history.
Women officers required to undertake to resign on marriage. LO-112 exactly - a cause and consequence of the disadvantage faced by women.
Defence and foreign affairs as exclusively Union subjects, against local drainage and State police. Division of responsibility between tiers, LO-109.
Decentralisation as spreading power across levels rather than concentrating it. LO-109 exactly.
Judicial review as the court testing laws and government action against the Constitution. Goal-level CG-SST3 for an institution of democracy; the frame has no judiciary LO.
District Education Officers and the permanent executive delivering school toilets and teacher training on the ground. LO-115, the functioning of a government office in one's locality.

RTI empowering citizens to demand information on government action and spending. LO-115 for the office a citizen holds to account, LO-113 for the public scrutiny of government that information enables.
The 1970 Silent Valley dam threatening evergreen forest. LO-100 for conservation of flora and fauna, LO-108 because the chapter uses it as a public issue citizens contested.

The police as the State's lawful user of force for public safety. Goal-level CG-SST3 for an organ of the state; LO-115 is rejected because the item is about authority, not about a citizen dealing with an office.
NGOs, scientists and locals mobilising opinion until the Centre intervened at Silent Valley. LO-108 for citizens acting on a public issue, LO-100 for the forest that was saved.
Accountability as the duty of those in power to answer for their actions. Goal-level CG-SST3 for a principle of democratic working; no LO names it.
The Centre cancelling the dam in 1983 and declaring Silent Valley a National Park. LO-100 for the conservation outcome, LO-108 for the public pressure that produced it.
The IAS as an example of a bureaucratic service, against the courts and legislatures. LO-115, the permanent machinery that runs government offices.
The early-1990s amendments creating panchayats and municipalities as the third tier. LO-109 exactly - the constitutional basis of local government.

Villagers turning to the judiciary when a factory poisons their water and the local administration ignores them. CG-SST3 for the courts as the organ that protects rights, LO-108 because the scenario is a local issue read through rights.
A Bagepalli citizen filing an RTI to get the roadwork accounts and force repairs. LO-115 for holding a local office to account, LO-108 for acting on an issue in one's own region.
The judiciary as the organ that settles disputes and ensures laws are followed. Goal-level CG-SST3; the frame has no judiciary LO.
Why even a democracy needs constitutional limits - elected majorities can pass tyrannical laws. LO-106, the significance of equal protection in a democracy.
Muthamma naming religious tolerance and freedom of thought as what makes Indian democracy possible. CG-SST3 for the working of democracy, LO-106 for the equal standing of belief it rests on.
The Supreme Court striking down service rules that forced women to resign on marriage. LO-112 exactly - the consequence of a disadvantage faced by women, remedied through the right to equality.
Photographing a rubbish-filled park and tagging municipal officials on social media. LO-113 for media as the lever, LO-115 for the local office being pressed.
The three functions of government - making laws, carrying out policy, ensuring laws are followed. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the organs of government.
The four elements of a state - people, land, government, sovereignty. Goal-level CG-SST3.
'Land' as the state's defined territory. Goal-level CG-SST3; CG-SST1 is rejected because this is the political concept of territory, not physical geography.

Mapped on its stem, which asks what sovereignty means for a state. Goal-level CG-SST3, matching the other sovereignty item. (The stored answer is an advertising line plus stray option text; see report.)

This row's stem is a question and its answer run together; the scored content is what its answer gives - transparency as open access to how government decides and spends. CG-SST3 for the democratic principle, LO-115 for the offices whose spending is opened up. (Merged stem; see report.)
Checks and balances keeping any one organ from dominating. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the working of the Constitution.
Policy as a decided set of actions to address an issue. Goal-level CG-SST3 for how government works; no LO covers policy.
President and Prime Minister both in the political executive, the first largely formal, the second operational. Goal-level CG-SST3 for the institutions of Indian democracy.
State as permanent organisation, government as the temporary system running it. Goal-level CG-SST3, matching the other state-versus-government items.
